scope: Source-based English/Lean correspondence, simplification, strengthening and focused primary-source novelty review. This is separate from kernel verification and is not a global priority certificate.
headline_findings: BIT implies canonical WORD: one native machine depends only on the given bit machine, with raw input, blank initial workspace, exact output and actual halting. No schedule, reset, supplied counter, or dimension-advice premise survives.

The geometric and scan conclusions concern the exact public grammars defined in the manuscript. Public layouts/tables may depend on dimension but not payload. They are not normal forms for unrestricted multitape machines.

Every numbered English result is supported by its mapped Lean statement. Positive-dimension normalizations and full-Boolean-cube correctness are explicit. All original headline conclusions are preserved or strengthened.
strengthenings: Good image/predecessor-bin bound: 16 to 11; path coverage KL/m + K*11^L/B0.
Named helper: |F| <= (D+1)*h, replacing 2^(D+1)*h. Local determination is required only on F.
Scan ancestry D=(11*q)^L and record budget E_B+s*L*n, omitting the unused terminal-state field.
Path, circuit and scan exclusions hold at every positive multiple of a fixed dyadic threshold; former dyadic statements are derived corollaries.
simplifications: Reused mathlib finite-set union/image/filter identities and consolidated the generic bin-diameter estimate.
Replaced the half-marking helper framework by one finite-order acyclic-selection proof, with narrow imports; removed the superseded weighted experiment.

Removed unused native interpreter visit/origin tracks and the marker phase. Interpreter ports fall from 3*r+4 to r+2, where r is the work-track count after the five-symbol encoding, and a simulated macro from r+3 to r+2 transitions; final halt discovery remains charged.
NativeBootstrap.jump reuses NativeIO.jump_trace. The six-module native cleanup deletes 43 source lines; replay semantics and headline premises are preserved.
Second pass: removed four unused geometry declarations and reused the mathlib filter-union/complement identity, deleting a net 48 lines across three modules without changing any mapped endpoint.
clarifications: The contrapositive transfers failure of linear-time WORD to failure of linear-time BIT, not arbitrary quantitative lower bounds.
The shared helper counts distinct original coordinates over the full Boolean cube. Only named demands need determination; their own bins cannot be local side information.
Exceptional records contain current intermediate bits at bad source positions, which need not be raw input bits. Actual inherited entering states are charged.
The address-field conjugation and descending-rank helper reconstruction are explained explicitly in English.
Pointwise nonlinear gates are already covered by path unrolling; the additional scan argument charges information carried between addresses.

novelty_review.finding: The focused search did not locate the exact adaptive, uniform, raw-input canonical linear-time implication. No unqualified priority claim is made.
novelty_review.established_ingredients: Address-permutation factorization, Bennett history/replay and acyclic index-coding decoding are established methods and are attributed. The contribution claimed is the exact native reduction and the derived common-scale/helper bounds for the specified compiler grammar.

comparisons.source: Harvey and van der Hoeven, arXiv:2503.22848v1, Section 7.6
comparisons.finding: Discusses arbitrary-width complexity comparisons and provides an oblivious bit-to-word simulation. The present theorem is adaptive but restricted to canonical width and the linear-time regime.

comparisons.source: Bar-Yossef, Birk, Jayram and Kol, Index Coding with Side Information, 2011; Theorem 7
comparisons.finding: The acyclic induced-subgraph method underlies the helper argument; it is not a new general information principle.
History, retained output and reverse cleanup are established. Their literal paid realization is checked in the native model.
Indivisible-entry restriction differs from the nonlinear scan grammar; neither comparison implies a general tape lower bound.

comparisons.source: Adler et al., On the Capacity of Information Networks, 2006, Section 6
comparisons.finding: Conditional I/O/coding comparison has a different model. The present unconditional result has additional grammar restrictions.

comparisons.source: Krishnamoorthy et al., On Efficient Out-of-core Matrix Transposition, Technical Report OSU-CISRC-9/03-TR52, September 2003, Section 4
comparisons.finding: Precedent for address-bit factorization; different memory model and no matching adaptive native implication located.

novelty_review.limitations: Focused search only; incomplete indexing, inaccessible sources and recent work can leave overlaps undiscovered.

remaining_open: Unrestricted WORD implies BIT, existence of an unrestricted linear-time bit or word transposer, and barriers for arbitrary asynchronous schedules, adaptive layouts, growing depth/state or workspace.
